slides.title: "If AI can write it, AI can **handle it**."
paras: Reality: AI is great at first drafts, sorting and formatting. It doesn't know your costs, your clients or the rules where you work.
So keep the decision. Hand over the busywork around it.

steps.d: AI doesn't know your costs or margins.
Rules depend on where you are. Ask a pro.
A fair call needs your judgment and your name.
Hours, stock, policies: it guesses if you don't paste them.

before.label: DON'T HAND OVER
before.text:
"Write me a quote for repainting a 3-bedroom house."
AI can only guess the prices, or leave blanks.

after.label: AUTOMATE INSTEAD
after.text:
"Here are my line items and prices: [PASTE]. Turn them into a clear quote with scope, what's not included and payment terms."
You set the numbers. AI does the layout.

cards.title: Questions for your accountant
cards.text: I run a [TYPE OF BUSINESS] in [STATE/COUNTRY]. I'm meeting my accountant about [TOPIC]. Don't give me tax advice. List the 6 questions I should ask, in plain English, and the documents to bring.

cards.title: Same swap for legal stuff
cards.text: I need a lawyer's view on [CONTRACT OR ISSUE]. Don't tell me what the law says. List what I should ask and what to have ready, so the call is short.

slides.note: AI preps the meeting. The professional gives the answer.

messages.text: Small bakery. Topic: hiring my first part-time employee.

1. What must be set up before the first payday?
2. What does an employee cost on top of wages?
3. Employee or contractor for this role?
4. How should I track hours and breaks?
5. Which records do I keep, and for how long?
6. Does this change my tax payments?
**Bring:** last year's return, your profit and loss, the role's hours and pay.

before.label: DON'T HAND OVER
before.text: Pasting an AI apology straight to a client whose order you got wrong. It reads polished, not sorry.

after.label: AUTOMATE INSTEAD
after.text:
"Give me 3 talking points and 3 phrases to avoid for telling [CLIENT] that [WHAT WENT WRONG]."
Then call, or write it in your own words.

slides.note: AI drafts. You decide, check and send.

caption:
5 tasks you shouldn't hand to AI (and what to automate instead)

AI is great at drafts, sorting and formatting. It doesn't know your costs, your clients or the rules where you work. So keep these 5 for yourself: final prices, tax and legal answers, hard news to a client, hiring decisions and facts about your business.

Then hand over the busywork around them. My favorite swap, for tax and legal stuff:

"I run a [TYPE OF BUSINESS] in [STATE/COUNTRY]. I'm meeting my accountant about [TOPIC]. Don't give me tax advice. List the 6 questions I should ask, in plain English, and the documents to bring."

You walk into the meeting prepared, and the professional gives the actual answer.

Same idea for quotes: you type the prices, AI does the layout. For bad news: AI gives you talking points, you say it in your own words.
